arm_traffic.scope: Actual compiled ARM control + deterministic desktop traffic; no physical board or GPU emulation
checks: scheduled-brake: ARM AEB overrides held accelerator
scheduled-brake: active mode avoids collision in this defined test
scheduled-brake: warning-only alerts with no actuator output
scheduled-brake: ignoring warning permits collision
scheduled-brake: off suppresses alerts and actuator output
scheduled-brake: unassisted held accelerator permits collision
scheduled-brake: warning/off physics match for the same player inputs
constant-slow-target: ARM AEB overrides held accelerator
constant-slow-target: active mode avoids collision in this defined test
constant-slow-target: warning-only alerts with no actuator output
constant-slow-target: ignoring warning permits collision
constant-slow-target: off suppresses alerts and actuator output
constant-slow-target: unassisted held accelerator permits collision
constant-slow-target: warning/off physics match for the same player inputs
Runner pause clears card output and stops at acknowledged step
Resume retains road/traffic and accepts nonzero first timestamp after RESET
Card warning-mode touch action is returned through J
Card START request is visible to the host
Card mode selection is locked during a run
Card PAUSE request is visible to the host
Maximum sample fields and sequence fit the real ARM parser/formatter
All game command/reply sizes respect existing UART buffers

physical_game.scope: Physical STM32 UART/controller/GPU; simulated traffic and driver inputs
checks: Physical ADASLab v2 runs under DeviceBoot v2
Active AEB brakes against held W and avoids defined braking traffic
active: real GPU completion and LCD frame counters advance
active: pause clears physical controller output
Warning mode alerts without applying the brake
warn: real GPU completion and LCD frame counters advance
warn: pause clears physical controller output
Off mode suppresses warnings and intervention
off: real GPU completion and LCD frame counters advance
off: pause clears physical controller output
Physical ACC accelerates toward target with no pedals pressed
Physical controller rejects duplicate timestamps
Physical controller rejects damaged sample CRC
Physical controller clears output when data stops

limitations: Physical finger gestures were not automated; exact LVGL touch action functions were exercised in compiled ARM tests.
Windows launcher was reviewed but not executed on Windows.
Traffic is simulated; this is an educational control model.
